faq: Is FrankenPHP a drop-in replacement for PHP-FPM?
Mostly, in classic mode: your code runs per request as it does under FPM. You need a thread-safe PHP build, and a few extensions such as imap, newrelic and pcov are not supported.

In worker mode it usually is, because the app boots once instead of on every request. In classic mode the gain is small. If your requests are slow because of database queries, neither runtime will fix that.
Do I still need nginx with FrankenPHP?
No. FrankenPHP is built on Caddy and serves HTTP, HTTPS with automatic certificates, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 itself. Some teams keep a load balancer in front for other reasons.
What is the biggest risk when moving to FrankenPHP?
Worker mode state leaks and the larger crash blast radius. Migrate to classic mode first, run under a supervisor, then adopt worker mode once your code is safe across requests.
